task_2.title: Add Clang 20 compiler setting support
task_2.description: Conan 2.14.0 adds user-facing support for Clang 20 by recognizing it as a valid `compiler.version` value for the `clang` compiler setting. This lets users declare and use Clang 20 toolchains in normal package workflows without the configuration being rejected as unsupported.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan accepts Clang 20 as a supported `compiler.version` for the `clang` compiler so users can configure, install, and create packages with Clang 20 toolchains.

expectation.grounded: When `settings.compiler=clang`, Conan must recognize `settings.compiler.version=20` as a valid public setting value anywhere Conan settings are consumed, including profiles and command-line settings for package workflows. The upgrade should remove invalid-setting failures that occur only because Clang 20 was previously unknown.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to select Clang 20 in Conan the same way they select other supported Clang versions, and Conan should treat that compiler choice as supported during normal package operations.

constraints.grounded: Existing accepted `clang` version values must remain valid, and the change must only expand support to include version `20` rather than altering the meaning of other compiler settings or introducing new required configuration for Clang users.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should add support for the new compiler release without regressing existing compiler-version handling or changing how current supported Clang configurations behave.

behavior: Conan accepts `clang` version `20` as a valid compiler setting value.
Profiles or command-line settings that specify Clang 20 are treated as supported configuration instead of being rejected for using an unknown `clang` version.
Package workflows that rely on Conan settings validation can proceed with Clang 20 under the same settings model already used for earlier supported Clang releases.
Previously supported Clang versions remain available and unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: When a user sets `compiler=clang` and `compiler.version=20`, Conan should accept the configuration as valid.
When a profile declares Clang 20, Conan should parse and use that profile without failing solely because version 20 is unsupported.
When package creation or installation is run with Clang 20 settings, Conan should not raise an invalid compiler-version error caused only by the version value `20`.
When users continue using already supported Clang versions, behavior should remain unchanged.

task_4.title: Add validate lifecycle hooks for recipe validation
task_4.description: Version 2.14.0 adds hook support around recipe validation so external integrations can inject validation behavior before and after a recipe's validate() execution without modifying the recipe itself. The update also ensures these hooks participate in the normal package ID evaluation flow and remain aligned with invalid-configuration handling.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan exposes lifecycle hooks around recipe validate() execution so CI and other integrations can apply additional validation logic during package evaluation without changing the recipe.

expectation.grounded: Conan 2.14.0 should recognize the hook entry points pre_validate and post_validate and execute them around a recipe's validate() method when validate() is defined. These hooks should run through the configured HookManager during the same validation flow used for package ID computation and related graph/binary analysis. If validate() raises ConanInvalidConfiguration, the package should still be marked invalid through the existing validation flow rather than turning that condition into a generic failure, and post_validate should still execute after that invalidation path completes.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to attach custom logic immediately before and after recipe validation, allowing environment-specific validation policies to run automatically wherever Conan evaluates a recipe. Recipes that explicitly reject a configuration should continue to be treated as invalid configurations, while still allowing the post-validation hook to observe the completed validation outcome.

constraints.grounded: The new behavior must not introduce validate hooks for recipes that do not implement validate(). Existing hook phases for export, source, generate, build, and related operations must remain intact. The validate hook addition must preserve the current ConanInvalidConfiguration semantics used by validate(), including invalid package state propagation during package ID evaluation.
constraints.conceptual: The feature should extend validation observability without changing how unrelated lifecycle hooks behave or altering the meaning of an invalid recipe configuration. It should add hook coverage only where recipe validation actually exists.

behavior: Conan recognizes pre_validate and post_validate as valid hook lifecycle methods.
When a recipe defines validate(), Conan executes pre_validate before calling validate().
When a recipe defines validate(), Conan executes post_validate after validate() finishes.
If validate() raises ConanInvalidConfiguration, Conan records the recipe as invalid using the existing validation mechanism instead of treating that case as a generic runtime error.
If validate() raises ConanInvalidConfiguration, post_validate still runs after the invalid configuration has been recorded.
Recipes that do not define validate() do not trigger pre_validate or post_validate.
Validate hooks are available during the normal package evaluation path, including package ID computation and graph binary analysis that invoke recipe validation.
acceptance_criteria: When a recipe implements validate() and Conan evaluates that recipe, it should invoke pre_validate before validate() and post_validate after validate().
When a recipe implements validate() and validate() rejects the configuration with ConanInvalidConfiguration, the recipe should be treated as invalid rather than as an unexpected failure.
When validate() rejects the configuration with ConanInvalidConfiguration, post_validate should still be invoked after the invalid result is recorded.
When a recipe does not implement validate(), Conan should not invoke pre_validate or post_validate for that recipe.
When Conan performs package graph or package ID evaluation that runs recipe validation, the same pre_validate and post_validate hook behavior should be available there as well.

task_1.title: Add conan audit vulnerability scanning
task_1.description: Conan 2.14.0 adds a new `conan audit` security workflow that can inspect package references or resolved dependency graphs for known vulnerabilities through configurable providers, including provider management, authentication, and text/JSON/HTML reporting.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan users can audit package references and dependency graphs for known vulnerabilities through a new `conan audit` workflow, configure and authenticate the vulnerability provider they want to use, and receive clear results when vulnerabilities, missing packages, authentication issues, or rate limits are encountered.

expectation.grounded: Expose a `conan audit` command group with `scan`, `list`, and `provider` subcommands. `conan audit scan` must resolve the dependency graph from Conan graph inputs and query the selected provider, defaulting to `conancenter`. `conan audit list` must accept either one recipe reference or a pkglist through `-l/--list` and optionally `-r/--remote`, while rejecting missing input or simultaneous reference and list input. `conan audit provider` must support `add`, `list`, `auth`, and `remove` for provider types `conan-center-proxy` and `private`, with persisted tokens, environment-variable token override via `CONAN_AUDIT_PROVIDER_TOKEN_<PROVIDER_NAME>`, and provider lookup/authentication failures surfaced as `ConanException`. Audit results must be available in text, JSON, and HTML formats and expose per-package vulnerability data, severity, totals, and clean-scan cases.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to run a built-in audit command to check either a dependency graph or explicit package references for known CVEs, choose or manage the security provider used for the lookup, authenticate once or override credentials from the environment, and get readable or machine-consumable output that distinguishes clean scans from vulnerable, missing, unauthorized, or rate-limited responses.

constraints.grounded: Keep the feature additive to existing Conan workflows. `conancenter` must be available as the default audit provider, invalid input combinations for `audit list` must fail before any query is sent, duplicate provider names and unsupported provider types must be rejected, and provider names must not contain spaces. Missing packages returned by the Conan Center proxy must be reported as warnings for the affected reference without aborting other results, while authorization failures, rate limiting, internal server errors, corrupted stored tokens, and other provider errors must stop the audit as an error condition.
constraints.conceptual: The audit capability should be opt-in and predictable: invalid user input should fail early, provider configuration should be explicit, clean and vulnerable results should both be clearly reported, unavailable catalog entries should not hide successful results for other packages, and fatal provider or authentication failures should not be presented as successful audits.

behavior: `conan audit scan` resolves a dependency graph and audits the dependency package references against the selected provider or the default `conancenter` provider.
`conan audit list` audits either a single package reference or the references contained in a pkglist file, and it raises an input error if the user provides neither input or both inputs together.

`conan audit provider add`, `list`, `auth`, and `remove` manage audit providers, with `add` requiring a provider name, URL, and supported provider type, and `add` or `auth` accepting a token interactively or through `--token`.
If no provider configuration exists yet, the public `conancenter` provider is created by default as a `conan-center-proxy` provider pointed at the public audit service.

When no token is available for the default public provider, an audit request fails before querying and requires provider authentication; when a stored token is malformed, provider retrieval fails; when `CONAN_AUDIT_PROVIDER_TOKEN_<PROVIDER_NAME>` is set, that token overrides the stored credential.

Audit output is available in text, JSON, and HTML formats; successful results show vulnerabilities grouped by package, sorted by severity order (`Critical`, `High`, `Medium`, `Low`), include CVSS and references when present, and clearly report clean packages and total vulnerability counts.

A package that is not available from the Conan Center vulnerability source produces a warning for that reference without aborting the whole audit, while authorization failures, rate limits, internal server errors, and other provider failures stop the audit and report an error.
acceptance_criteria: When a user runs `conan audit scan` on a recipe or explicit requirements, it should resolve dependencies and return vulnerability information for the resulting packages through the chosen provider.

When a user runs `conan audit list <reference>`, it should validate the reference and return vulnerability data for that package; when the user passes `-l/--list`, it should audit the package references described by that pkglist instead.
When a user invokes `conan audit list` with neither a reference nor a pkglist, or with both at once, the command should fail with an input error instead of running an audit.
When a user has not authenticated the default `conancenter` provider, an audit request against that provider should fail and require authentication before the audit can proceed.
When `CONAN_AUDIT_PROVIDER_TOKEN_<PROVIDER_NAME>` is defined, audit requests should use that token in preference to any stored token for the same provider.
When vulnerabilities are found, text, JSON, and HTML output should expose them per package with severity information; when none are found, the output should clearly indicate a clean result.

When one requested package is unavailable from the public Conan Center vulnerability source, the command should warn for that package and continue reporting other results; when the provider returns authorization, rate-limit, or server failures, the command should stop and report the audit as failed.

task_3.title: Selective workspace install by editable path
task_3.description: Conan 2.14.0 extends `workspace install` so users can optionally pass one or more editable package paths and install only that subset of the workspace instead of always processing every editable package. This reduces installation scope for large workspaces while preserving the existing full-workspace behavior when no paths are provided.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `workspace install` can target only the selected editable packages in a workspace when one or more package paths are provided, instead of always installing the entire workspace.

expectation.grounded: `workspace install` must accept zero or more positional path arguments. When paths are provided, Conan must resolve those paths to workspace editables and use only the selected editable packages as the install roots. When no paths are provided, `workspace install` must continue to install all editable packages in the workspace. If the effective selection contains no editable packages, the command must fail with a ConanException instead of proceeding.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to run `workspace install` for just the part of a workspace they are actively working on by naming one or more editable package paths. A normal `workspace install` with no extra paths should still behave like a full workspace install. The command should not silently succeed when there is nothing installable in the requested scope.

constraints.grounded: Partial installation must only narrow the set of editable root packages considered by `workspace install`; it must not change the default full-workspace behavior when no paths are supplied. Unselected workspace editables must not be included as install roots for a filtered invocation. The command must keep enforcing the existing failure behavior when no editable packages are available after selection.
constraints.conceptual: This feature is a scoped install option, not a change to how full workspace installs work. Selecting a subset should avoid pulling in unrelated workspace packages as top-level install targets, and empty selections should still be treated as an error.

behavior: `workspace install` now accepts optional positional path arguments representing editable packages in the workspace.
When one or more paths are supplied, the install operation filters the workspace editables to that selection before building the install graph.
When no paths are supplied, the command preserves the prior behavior of installing all editable packages in the workspace.
A filtered install only includes dependencies reachable from the selected editable roots, so unrelated workspace editables are excluded from the install scope.
If no editable packages remain after resolving the requested install scope, the command raises a ConanException instead of running an empty install.
acceptance_criteria: When a workspace contains multiple editable packages and the user runs `workspace install` without path arguments, it should install the workspace using all editables as before.
When the user runs `workspace install <path>` for an editable package in the workspace, it should install only that selected editable package and the dependencies required from that selection.
When the user runs `workspace install <path1> <path2>`, it should treat both selected editables as the install roots and limit the install scope to that combined subset.
When some workspace editables are not selected in a partial install, they should not be included as top-level install targets for that invocation.
When the requested install scope resolves to no editable packages, the command should fail rather than completing successfully with no install roots.

task_6.title: Support Apple package frameworks in CMakeConfigDeps
task_6.description: Conan 2.14.0 extends CMakeConfigDeps so Apple frameworks are represented correctly in generated CMake package targets. Packages can now declare packaged frameworks through cpp_info.package_framework, and existing cpp_info.frameworks entries are translated into framework link flags instead of being ignored by the new generator.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to Conan 2.14.0 lets Apple framework packages be consumed correctly through CMakeConfigDeps, including both packaged frameworks exported by a dependency and Apple system frameworks declared in package metadata.

expectation.grounded: CMakeConfigDeps must accept a new cpp_info.package_framework value on cpp_info and component cpp_info objects, and when it is present it must generate an imported CMake target for the framework using cpp_info.location and cpp_info.type. Entries declared in cpp_info.frameworks must be propagated as Apple framework link dependencies instead of being reported as unsupported. Target generation must also proceed when a package exposes only package_framework or system_libs metadata and no regular libs.
expectation.conceptual: Consumers using CMakeConfigDeps should be able to depend on Apple frameworks the same way they depend on normal Conan packages: generated CMake package targets should carry the right framework linkage and framework-specific metadata so builds work without special manual wiring.

constraints.grounded: Using cpp_info.package_framework requires a valid cpp_info.location for the framework binary, and the generated CMake target must preserve the package's shared vs static nature through cpp_info.type. Existing non-framework library handling, including the single-library restriction already enforced by the new CMakeDeps generator, must remain unchanged.
constraints.conceptual: The new framework support must not break existing non-framework package consumption, and framework packages must still provide enough metadata for consumers to resolve the actual framework artifact and link model safely.

behavior: A new cpp_info.package_framework field is available to describe a packaged Apple framework separately from cpp_info.frameworks.
CMakeConfigDeps no longer treats cpp_info.frameworks as unsupported; it emits the corresponding Apple framework link dependency on the generated target.
When cpp_info.package_framework is declared, CMakeConfigDeps generates an imported framework target whose imported location comes from cpp_info.location.
Framework package targets derive their imported library kind from cpp_info.type so shared and static framework packages are represented consistently in generated CMake metadata.
When a package framework is declared, generated metadata treats headers as framework-provided rather than exposing normal include directories for that target.
For package frameworks, generated CMake metadata includes the framework search information needed for compatible CMake consumption, including older supported CMake versions.
Packages that only expose system libraries or a package framework are still emitted as CMake targets instead of being skipped.
If cpp_info.package_framework is set without cpp_info.location, CMakeConfigDeps fails during generation rather than emitting incomplete framework metadata.
acceptance_criteria: When a package declares cpp_info.package_framework together with cpp_info.location and is consumed via CMakeConfigDeps on Apple platforms, the generated package target should behave as an imported framework target and resolve the packaged framework binary correctly.
When a package declares cpp_info.frameworks, a consumer linking the generated CMake target should also link the declared Apple system frameworks without manual additions.
When a package exposes only cpp_info.package_framework or only cpp_info.system_libs, CMakeConfigDeps should still generate a usable package target.
When cpp_info.package_framework is declared without cpp_info.location, package generation should fail with an explicit framework-metadata error instead of silently producing broken CMake files.
When consuming existing non-framework packages through CMakeConfigDeps, their normal library behavior should remain unchanged after the upgrade.

task_5.title: Add Apple framework support to CMakeConfigDeps
task_5.description: The upgrade makes Apple frameworks first-class outputs in CMakeConfigDeps. Packages can now expose packaged frameworks, system frameworks, and framework search directories through Conan metadata so generated CMake config files resolve and link framework-based dependencies correctly without requiring them to masquerade as ordinary libraries.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that CMakeConfigDeps fully supports Apple framework-based dependencies, including packaged frameworks, system frameworks, and framework search paths, so consumers can use framework-only packages without extra manual integration metadata.

expectation.grounded: When a dependency consumed through CMakeConfigDeps publishes cpp_info.package_framework, cpp_info.location, cpp_info.frameworks, or cpp_info.frameworkdirs, the generated CMake package metadata should expose the dependency as a usable Apple framework target, link declared system frameworks, and prepend framework search directories through CMAKE_FRAMEWORK_PATH. Dependencies that only export a package framework or framework-related metadata must still produce usable consumer metadata. If cpp_info.package_framework is declared, cpp_info.location is required.
expectation.conceptual: Consumers using CMakeConfigDeps should be able to consume Apple framework dependencies the same way they consume other Conan packages: packaged frameworks should link correctly, required system frameworks should no longer be ignored, and framework search locations should be available automatically. Invalid framework exports should fail clearly instead of producing incomplete package metadata.

constraints.grounded: Framework support must not require packages to invent placeholder cpp_info.libs entries or duplicate normal include directory metadata for framework headers. Existing non-framework CMakeConfigDeps behavior for regular libraries and search paths should remain intact. Declaring cpp_info.package_framework without a framework location is invalid and must not generate incomplete targets.
constraints.conceptual: The new capability should extend framework handling without regressing ordinary package consumption. Framework packages should work from their own metadata rather than from workarounds, and malformed framework declarations should be rejected instead of partially accepted.

behavior: CMakeConfigDeps now translates declared Apple system frameworks into consumer link information instead of warning that frameworks are unsupported.
A package that declares cpp_info.package_framework is emitted as an imported CMake framework target using its published location, even when it does not expose a conventional library name.
Framework-only packages are treated as valid consumer dependencies, so generated metadata is still produced when the dependency metadata contains framework information without ordinary libs.
Framework package targets rely on framework semantics for header exposure instead of propagating standard include directories as if the package were a normal library.
Published framework search directories are added to generated CMAKE_FRAMEWORK_PATH so framework discovery works for host and test dependencies.
For older CMake releases, generated metadata preserves compatibility by supplying the framework search option needed for C and C++ compilation against packaged frameworks.
acceptance_criteria: When a Conan dependency declares an Apple package framework and its location, a consumer using CMakeConfigDeps should be able to link the generated dependency target without the package also declaring a normal library name.
When a dependency declares Apple system frameworks, consumers linking the generated dependency target should receive those framework link requirements automatically.

When a dependency publishes framework search directories, the generated CMake configuration should expose them through CMAKE_FRAMEWORK_PATH so dependent framework resolution succeeds without extra manual path setup.
When a framework package is consumed on an older supported CMake version, consumers should still be able to compile against the framework without manually adding framework search flags.
When cpp_info.package_framework is declared without a corresponding framework location, dependency generation should fail with a Conan error instead of producing incomplete package metadata.

task_8.title: Improve Conan Jinja2 Profile Syntax Error Reporting
task_8.description: Conan 2.14.0 improves how profile loading reports failures when a Jinja2-based profile contains invalid syntax. Syntax errors that occur while preparing or rendering a profile template are now surfaced through Conan's profile error flow with the relevant profile context, including when the broken profile is reached through included profiles.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that invalid Jinja2 syntax in Conan profile templates fails with a clear profile-rendering error tied to the affected profile, including when the faulty template is loaded indirectly through profile includes.

expectation.grounded: When Conan loads a profile that uses Jinja2 templating, failures raised while parsing or rendering the template should be converted into Conan's profile-rendering error path rather than escaping as an unwrapped Jinja2 parser exception. The observable failure should identify the profile template being processed, preserve the underlying syntax/rendering cause, and continue to propagate through existing profile include handling such as include()-based chains.
expectation.conceptual: Users should get a consistent Conan profile error whenever a templated profile is malformed, with enough context to see which profile caused the failure and why, even if that profile was pulled in by another profile.

constraints.grounded: Valid Jinja2 profiles and normal profile include resolution must continue to behave as before. This change is limited to error handling for template parse/render failures and should not alter successful profile evaluation, include semantics, or replace the original failure cause with a generic silent failure.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should improve failure clarity without changing how working profiles load or how profile inclusion behaves in successful cases.

behavior: A malformed Jinja2 profile template is treated as a Conan profile rendering failure instead of surfacing as an unwrapped template parser error.
The reported failure is associated with the specific profile template Conan was processing when the error occurred.
Underlying Jinja2 syntax or rendering details remain visible as part of the Conan error so users can diagnose the template issue.

If the malformed profile is reached through one or more included profiles, the failure continues through Conan's existing profile-reading context so the include chain remains observable to the caller.
acceptance_criteria: When a command loads a profile whose Jinja2 template contains invalid syntax, it should fail with a Conan profile-rendering error that points to the affected profile rather than exposing a raw template parser exception.

When the invalid Jinja2 template is referenced by another profile through profile inclusion, the command should still fail through Conan's profile-loading error flow and retain the original template failure details.
When a profile template fails during parsing or rendering, the user-visible error should provide both profile context and the underlying cause so the broken Jinja2 content can be identified.
When profiles are valid, profile loading and inclusion behavior should remain unchanged by this update.

task_9.title: Suppress false auto-deduce warnings for exact library matches
task_9.description: The upgrade refines automatic library location deduction so that Conan no longer emits an ambiguity warning when multiple matching files are found but the resolved library file is already an exact match for the requested library name, including the common lib-prefixed form. Warnings remain for genuinely ambiguous matches.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that automatic library location deduction does not warn users about multiple matches when the resolved library file is already an exact match for the requested library name, while preserving warnings for genuinely ambiguous matches.

expectation.grounded: During automatic deduction of a library location from multiple filesystem matches, the library should still resolve to the selected match, but warning output should be suppressed when the resolved file basename exactly matches the requested library name or the same name with the standard `lib` prefix. If the resolved basename is not an exact match in either form, the existing multiple-match warning should still be emitted.
expectation.conceptual: When Conan can clearly identify the intended library from the available files, it should resolve it quietly instead of reporting a misleading ambiguity warning. Users should still be warned when the available matches remain meaningfully ambiguous.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the existing auto-deduction flow for selecting and returning the library location beyond suppressing false-positive warnings for exact-name matches. Continue warning when multiple candidates exist and the resolved candidate name differs from the requested library name except for neither an exact match nor a `lib`-prefixed exact match.
constraints.conceptual: Limit the change to warning behavior for clearly identifiable matches. Keep location deduction behavior stable and retain warnings for cases that are still ambiguous from a user perspective.

behavior: If automatic library location deduction finds multiple candidate files, it continues to resolve a library location from the candidate set.
If the resolved candidate's filename, excluding its extension, exactly matches the requested library name, no multiple-match warning is emitted.
If the resolved candidate's filename, excluding its extension, matches the requested library name with a leading `lib` prefix, no multiple-match warning is emitted.
If multiple candidates are found and the resolved candidate name is not an exact match in either of those forms, a multiple-match warning is still emitted.
acceptance_criteria: When automatic library location deduction encounters multiple candidate files for a requested library and the resolved file basename exactly matches the requested library name, it should return the resolved location without emitting a multiple-match warning.

When automatic library location deduction encounters multiple candidate files for a requested library and the resolved file basename matches the requested library name only by the standard `lib` prefix, it should return the resolved location without emitting a multiple-match warning.

When automatic library location deduction encounters multiple candidate files and the resolved file basename is not an exact match for the requested library name in either exact or `lib`-prefixed form, it should still emit a multiple-match warning.
When this warning-suppression rule applies, it should not prevent the library location from being resolved and returned as usual.

task_11.title: Preserve Windows Paths in MSBuildDeps
task_11.description: The MSBuildDeps generator now preserves Windows path separators in generated MSBuild dependency metadata instead of normalizing them to forward slashes, fixing compatibility with MSBuild features that require native Windows-style paths.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that MSBuild dependency files generated by `MSBuildDeps` preserve Windows-style path separators so MSBuild features that depend on native `\` paths continue to work correctly.

expectation.grounded: `MSBuildDeps` should stop converting backslash-separated Windows paths to forward-slash form when emitting path values for generated MSBuild dependency metadata. Generated path values should continue to remove an unnecessary leading `/` prefix when present, but otherwise preserve the original Windows separator style so MSBuild can consume the paths as native Windows paths.
expectation.conceptual: Generated MSBuild dependency metadata should use Windows-native path formatting where applicable, so consumers can rely on the output with MSBuild functionality that expects standard Windows paths.

constraints.grounded: The fix is limited to path normalization behavior in `MSBuildDeps`: preserving backslashes must not introduce malformed leading `/` prefixes, and generated path values should remain valid for normal MSBuild consumption.
constraints.conceptual: Keep the change narrowly focused on path formatting. The generated files should remain usable by existing MSBuild workflows while avoiding path shapes that are invalid or unexpectedly rooted.

behavior: `MSBuildDeps` no longer rewrites `\` path separators to `/` when generating MSBuild dependency path values.
Generated MSBuild path values now preserve Windows-style separators so downstream MSBuild features can interpret them as native Windows paths.
If a generated path includes an unnecessary leading `/`, that prefix is still removed before the value is written.
acceptance_criteria: When `MSBuildDeps` generates dependency metadata containing Windows paths, the emitted values should keep `\` separators instead of converting them to `/`.

When generated MSBuild files are consumed by Windows MSBuild features that require native Windows paths, those features should be able to use the emitted dependency paths without separator-related failures.
When a generated path value contains a leading `/` that does not belong in the final MSBuild path, the output should omit that prefix while preserving the rest of the path.

task_10.title: Deprecate cmake_set_interface_link_directories in CMake dependency generators
task_10.description: Conan 2.14 removes the need to rely on the cmake_set_interface_link_directories package property for generated CMake dependency files. CMakeDeps now treats the property as legacy and stops adding extra root-target link-directory propagation for it, while CMakeConfigDeps warns that the property is invalid and expects package metadata to be fully described through normal package_info() declarations.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that packages upgrading to Conan 2.14 no longer depend on cmake_set_interface_link_directories for generated CMake dependency metadata, and that any use of this property is treated as deprecated for CMakeDeps and invalid for CMakeConfigDeps in favor of complete package_info() declarations.

expectation.grounded: If a recipe sets self.cpp_info.set_property("cmake_set_interface_link_directories", True), CMakeDeps should emit a deprecation warning and continue generating targets without using that property to append extra root-target INTERFACE_LINK_DIRECTORIES entries. CMakeConfigDeps should emit a deprecation or invalid-usage warning for the same property and require package_info() to provide the complete dependency and CPS-facing metadata instead of relying on that flag.
expectation.conceptual: The upgrade should make standard package metadata the only supported source of CMake dependency information. The old opt-in property may still be recognized for compatibility signals, but users should see that it is no longer needed in CMakeDeps and should not be used with CMakeConfigDeps.

constraints.grounded: Do not require cmake_set_interface_link_directories to expose normal include, link, or component metadata in generated CMake files. Existing component library-directory propagation in CMakeDeps should remain available through the usual package_info() libdirs data, and deprecation handling should surface as warnings rather than a hidden change in API shape.
constraints.conceptual: Packages that already describe their libraries and components correctly should keep generating usable CMake metadata. The change should only remove reliance on the legacy property and should not force consumers to adopt new behavior beyond using normal package declarations.

behavior: CMakeDeps recognizes cmake_set_interface_link_directories as a legacy boolean property and emits a deprecation warning when it is enabled.
In CMakeDeps, enabling cmake_set_interface_link_directories no longer causes the root generated target to append interface link directories from package libdirs solely because of that property.
In CMakeDeps, component targets continue to expose interface link directories from their declared component libdirs through normal generated target metadata, without requiring the legacy property.
CMakeConfigDeps emits a deprecation or invalid-usage warning when cmake_set_interface_link_directories is enabled and expects complete CMake/CPS-relevant metadata to come from package_info() instead.
acceptance_criteria: When a recipe enables cmake_set_interface_link_directories and generates files with CMakeDeps, generation should succeed, produce a deprecation warning, and avoid adding extra root-target interface link directories only because that property was set.

When a package defines components with library directories and uses CMakeDeps, the generated component targets should still expose those link directories through normal metadata without depending on cmake_set_interface_link_directories.

When a recipe enables cmake_set_interface_link_directories and generates files with CMakeConfigDeps, generation should surface that the property is deprecated or invalid and should rely on complete package_info() metadata rather than the property for dependency information.

task_12.title: Isolate local-recipes-index cache from workspace home_folder overrides
task_12.description: Version 2.14.0 fixes an issue where a workspace-level home_folder could incorrectly redefine the auxiliary cache used for local-recipes-index remotes. The update keeps that remote-specific cache isolated from workspace cache redirection and tightens the ConanAPI cache_folder contract to require absolute paths.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that using a local-recipes-index remote from within a workspace does not let the workspace home_folder redefine the remote's auxiliary cache location. Ensure that direct ConanAPI cache_folder configuration only accepts absolute paths.

expectation.grounded: When Conan interacts with a local-recipes-index remote, it should create and use that remote's auxiliary .conan cache under the local-recipes-index storage area, independent of any workspace home_folder setting. Recipe loading and hook resolution for that remote should use the isolated auxiliary cache rather than inheriting workspace cache redirection. Additionally, constructing ConanAPI with cache_folder set to a relative path should raise ConanException, while an absolute cache_folder remains valid and still has lower priority than a workspace-defined home_folder.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to work with a local recipes index remote even when a workspace relocates the main Conan home. The remote's internal metadata and cache should remain self-contained, and explicit API cache paths should be accepted only when they identify an unambiguous absolute location.

constraints.grounded: Do not allow workspace home_folder precedence to leak into the auxiliary cache used for local-recipes-index remotes. Preserve normal workspace precedence for the main Conan environment without redirecting the remote-specific local-recipes-index cache. Reject relative values passed to ConanAPI(cache_folder=...).
constraints.conceptual: Workspace configuration may change the main working environment, but it must not corrupt or relocate special-purpose remote storage. Cache path validation should reject ambiguous relative locations.

behavior: Commands that access a local-recipes-index remote use that remote's dedicated auxiliary .conan cache instead of a workspace-defined home folder.
Hook lookup and recipe loading for local-recipes-index operations resolve from the isolated auxiliary cache associated with the remote.
Using a workspace with home_folder no longer causes local-recipes-index remote access to be redirected to the wrong cache location.
ConanAPI(cache_folder=...) raises ConanException when the supplied cache_folder path is not absolute.
acceptance_criteria: Given a workspace that defines home_folder and a configured local-recipes-index remote, when Conan performs an operation against that remote, it should use the remote's own auxiliary cache and complete without being redirected by the workspace cache location.
When a workspace home_folder is configured, it should affect the main Conan environment but should not redefine the auxiliary .conan storage used by a local-recipes-index remote.
When recipe metadata or hooks are resolved for a local-recipes-index remote, they should come from the remote's isolated auxiliary cache context.
When ConanAPI is constructed with a relative cache_folder path, it should raise ConanException.
When ConanAPI is constructed with an absolute cache_folder path, it should accept the path subject to the documented precedence of a workspace-defined home_folder.

task_13.title: Preserve prepend order in environment profile dumps
task_13.description: Version 2.14.0 fixes environment profile serialization so dumped output preserves the intended order of prepended values, including path-style entries and mixed prepend/append definitions. This makes profile round-tripping stable and keeps the dumped environment semantics aligned with user-authored input.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that dumping environment definitions from profiles preserves the user-declared prepend order so serialized output reflects the intended environment composition for both regular and path variables.

expectation.grounded: When environment data is serialized through profile/environment dump APIs such as `ProfileEnvironment.dumps()`, entries defined with prepend syntax (`=+`) must be emitted in the same logical order they were declared by the user, rather than reversed. This applies to plain values and path-style entries, and mixed definitions must continue to place prepend operations before append operations in the dumped output.
expectation.conceptual: Serializing environment settings should round-trip user-authored prepend operations without reordering them. Users who load and re-dump a profile should see prepended values stay in the intended order, including when prepend and append operations are combined.

constraints.grounded: Do not change append (`+=`) serialization order or alter the existing separation between prepend and append operations in dumped output. The fix must apply consistently to both normal environment variables and path-oriented environment entries, and it must not change the meaning of other environment operations.
constraints.conceptual: Keep existing environment dump behavior intact except for correcting the order of prepended values. The output should remain stable for append-only cases and continue to distinguish prepends from appends correctly.

behavior: Dumped environment/profile output preserves the declared order of multiple prepend operations for the same variable.
The same ordering fix applies to path-style environment entries, not only scalar values.
When a variable contains both prepend and append operations, dumped output still lists prepends before appends while preserving each group's internal order.
Loading and then dumping a profile no longer reverses prepended entries during serialization.
acceptance_criteria: When a profile contains multiple prepended values for one environment variable and it is loaded then dumped, the dumped text should keep those prepended values in the same order they were declared.
When the same scenario uses path-style environment entries, the dumped output should preserve the declared prepend order there as well.
When a variable mixes prepend and append definitions, dumping should output prepend entries first and append entries afterward without reversing the order within either set.
When a variable uses only append definitions, dumping should continue to preserve append behavior unchanged.

task_7.title: Improve Docker runner platform, profile, and logging behavior
task_7.description: Conan 2.14.0 expands the Docker runner so users can choose a Docker build platform from runner configuration, correctly run projects whose recipe lives in a subfolder layout, use explicitly selected profiles even when they are outside the Conan home, and get standardized runner-prefixed logs during container execution.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the Docker runner supports explicit Docker platform selection, correctly mounts projects whose conanfile lives under a subfolder layout, resolves and stages the requested host and build profiles even when those profiles are outside the Conan home, and presents clearer runner execution logs without changing the basic Docker runner workflow.

expectation.grounded: The Docker runner must accept a `platform` setting from `[runner]` profile entries and from the runner config file `build.platform`, and pass that platform to Docker image builds. In `clean` and `copy` cache modes, it must resolve the profiles named by `-pr:h` and `-pr:b` through the profile API, copy those resolved profiles into the staged runner home, and stage the default build profile when no explicit build profile is supplied. When the consumer recipe defines a layout root above the current working directory, the runner must mount that root into the container and compute the container working path relative to it so recipes in subfolders remain accessible. Docker command output must be streamed through the runner logging path with a per-runner prefix, while invalid runner cache values still fail early and container command failures still surface as `ConanException` failures.
expectation.conceptual: Users configuring the Docker runner should be able to target a specific container architecture, run recipes from nested project layouts, and use their chosen profiles regardless of where those profile files live. Docker-runner execution should show readable, consistently prefixed live logs, and invalid runner configuration or failed container commands should still fail clearly.

constraints.grounded: The Docker runner must continue to require either a Dockerfile or an image, must continue to reject `format` output when running inside the Docker runner, and must preserve the existing cache modes `clean`, `copy`, and `shared` as the only accepted cache values. Existing runner configuration sources must remain supported: direct `[runner]` keys such as `dockerfile`, `build_context`, `image`, `configfile`, `cache`, `remove`, and `platform`, plus config-file driven container settings such as image, build arguments, cache sources, environment, volumes, user, privileges, and network.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade must extend Docker runner behavior without changing its core usage model. It should add compatibility for more Docker and profile scenarios, keep current cache mode semantics intact, and avoid regressing existing runner setup patterns.

behavior: A Docker runner profile can now specify the Docker build platform directly, and a runner config file can also provide the platform through its build section.

When the recipe layout declares a project root above the current directory, the Docker runner mounts that root instead of only the current folder and uses the correct in-container path for the recipe location.
In cache modes that stage configuration into the container, the runner copies the specific host and build profiles that were requested, including profiles resolved from paths outside the Conan home.
If no explicit build profile is provided, the runner stages the default build profile so container initialization still has a build profile available.

Runner command output is emitted live through a standardized runner log format with a runner-specific prefix instead of relying on boxed status messages and a trailing command-output dump only on failure.
Runner initialization validates cache mode values and rejects unsupported values before starting container execution.
acceptance_criteria: When a user sets Docker runner platform information in the profile or runner config file, the Docker image build should use that platform so cross-architecture runner setups are supported.

When `conan create` is invoked from a directory under a larger layout root, the Docker runner should mount the layout root and execute with a container path that still gives the recipe access to files above the current subfolder.
When host or build profiles are provided by name or by path outside the Conan home, Docker runner execution should still stage and use those profiles successfully.
When no build profile is explicitly passed in a staged-cache Docker runner workflow, the default build profile should still be available inside the container.
When a command runs inside the Docker runner, its output should appear as live runner-prefixed log lines, and a non-zero container command should still cause the overall Conan command to fail.
When the runner cache mode is not one of `clean`, `copy`, or `shared`, runner startup should fail before container work begins.

task_14.title: Support VCVars generation for WindowsStore targets
task_14.description: The upgrade fixes Conan's Microsoft VCVars generator so WindowsStore host configurations are recognized as valid Windows targets. Projects cross-building from Windows to WindowsStore should now receive the expected vcvars setup script instead of being treated as unsupported for generation.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the VCVars generator produces the expected Visual Studio environment setup script when the host operating system is WindowsStore and the build operating system is Windows.

expectation.grounded: When using the `VCVars` generator, Conan should generate `conanvcvars.bat` for host settings with `os=WindowsStore` as long as the build settings indicate `os=Windows`. The generated script should initialize the appropriate Visual C++ environment through `vcvarsall.bat`, including cross-compilation targets such as ARM64 when selected by the host architecture.
expectation.conceptual: Windows Store application targets should be handled like other Windows targets by the Visual Studio environment generator. Installing for a WindowsStore target from a Windows build machine should yield the same usable compiler setup script that users expect for Windows-based builds, including cross-target setups.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the requirement that VCVars generation depends on a Windows build machine. Non-Windows and non-WindowsStore host operating systems should remain outside this generator path, and standard Windows host behavior must remain unchanged.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should expand support only to the missing WindowsStore target case without broadening the feature to unrelated operating systems or altering existing Windows behavior.

behavior: A host configuration with `os=WindowsStore` is accepted by the `VCVars` generator instead of being filtered out as a non-Windows target.
If the build operating system is Windows, Conan generates the `conanvcvars.bat` environment script for WindowsStore targets.

The generated environment script continues to invoke the Visual Studio vcvars initialization flow appropriate for the selected target architecture, including Windows-to-ARM64 cross-compilation scenarios.
Configurations whose build operating system is not Windows remain ineligible for VCVars generation.
acceptance_criteria: When a consumer installs a package with the `VCVars` generator, a Windows build machine, and a host operating system of WindowsStore, Conan should generate `conanvcvars.bat`.
When the host architecture requires cross-compilation, such as ARM64, the generated VCVars script should target the corresponding Visual Studio cross environment rather than a generic native one.
When the host operating system is standard Windows, existing VCVars generation behavior should remain unchanged.
When the build operating system is not Windows, the VCVars generator should still refrain from producing the Windows Visual Studio setup script.

task_17.title: Detect user and channel conflicts in version-range dependency resolution
task_17.description: The 2.14.0 update fixes dependency graph conflict detection so version-range requirements are no longer treated as compatible when they refer to different package users or channels. Graph resolution now rejects these mismatched references consistently for both range-to-range and range-to-fixed comparisons.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that dependency graph resolution raises a conflict when requirements for the same package are compatible by version expression but differ by package user or channel, including cases where one or both requirements use a version range.

expectation.grounded: During dependency graph resolution, version-range handling must compare the requirement reference identity as well as version compatibility. If two competing requirements differ in `user` or `channel`, the resolver must raise `GraphConflictError` instead of intersecting version ranges or checking whether a concrete version is contained in a previous range. This applies when both requirements have `version_range` values and when only the previously seen requirement has a `version_range`.
expectation.conceptual: When Conan evaluates overlapping dependency requirements, package namespace differences must be treated as real conflicts. Requirements that point to different users or channels should fail resolution even if their versions or version ranges would otherwise match.

constraints.grounded: Existing non-conflicting behavior for requirements that share the same `user` and `channel` must remain unchanged, including version-range intersection and containment checks. Conflict detection must not depend on whether the current requirement or the previously resolved requirement is the one carrying the version range.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should only tighten incorrect acceptance of mismatched package identities. Compatible dependencies in the same namespace should continue resolving as before, and conflict detection should be consistent regardless of traversal order.

behavior: If two requirements for the same dependency are processed as version ranges and their references differ by `user` or `channel`, dependency graph construction raises a conflict immediately.

If a concrete requirement is compared against an already tracked version-range requirement and their references differ by `user` or `channel`, dependency graph construction raises a conflict before version containment is evaluated.
If competing requirements share the same `user` and `channel`, the resolver continues using version-range intersection or containment rules to decide compatibility.
The mismatch is surfaced as a dependency graph conflict during normal resolution instead of allowing the graph to proceed with an incorrect dependency selection.
acceptance_criteria: When two transitive requirements target the same package name with compatible version ranges but different users, installation should fail with a dependency conflict.
When two transitive requirements target the same package name with compatible version ranges but different channels, installation should fail with a dependency conflict.
When a fixed version requirement and a version-range requirement refer to different users or channels for the same package, installation should fail with a dependency conflict.
When competing requirements refer to the same user and channel, Conan should continue resolving them according to normal version-range compatibility rules.

task_16.title: Fix reduced recipe build-order to exclude non-build packages
task_16.description: The 2.14.0 update fixes `conan graph build-order` in reduced, recipe-ordered mode so the reported work set only contains package configurations that actually require building. This prevents reduced build-order output from listing non-build package entries under recipes that remain in the build plan.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that reduced, recipe-ordered `conan graph build-order` output only reports package configurations that still require a build, instead of keeping non-build packages under recipes that are otherwise part of the build order.

expectation.grounded: When `conan graph build-order` is requested with `--reduce` and recipe ordering, reduced `_InstallRecipeReference` results must keep the recipe reference and dependency structure but only expose package entries whose binary state is `Build` or `EditableBuild`. Package configurations with any other binary state must be filtered out from the recipe-level output. Reduced `_InstallConfiguration` entries that already represent a build-required package continue to be preserved.
expectation.conceptual: In reduced recipe-level build-order output, Conan should show only the package variants that actually need to be built. A recipe may still appear in the build order, but any package variant that does not require a build should be omitted from the reported work set.

constraints.grounded: Do not remove recipe entries that still have at least one build-required package. Preserve existing build-order relationships and keep package entries whose binary state is `Build` or `EditableBuild`. Do not surface package entries in reduced recipe-ordered output when their binary state is not build-required.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must narrow the reduced output without changing which recipes still require work. It should preserve the same build ordering while hiding package variants that are already satisfied or otherwise not scheduled to build.

behavior: Reduced recipe-ordered build-order output now filters each recipe's package list to build-required package variants only.
Package variants marked as `Build` remain visible in reduced output.
Package variants marked as `EditableBuild` remain visible in reduced output.
Package variants with any non-build binary state are omitted from reduced recipe-level build-order results.
Recipes that still require build work remain present in the reduced build order with their dependency relationships intact.
acceptance_criteria: When `conan graph build-order` is run with `--reduce` and recipe ordering for a recipe that has both build-required and non-build package variants, the output should include that recipe but list only the build-required package variants.
When a package variant is in binary state `Build`, it should appear in the reduced recipe-ordered build-order output.
When a package variant is in binary state `EditableBuild`, it should appear in the reduced recipe-ordered build-order output.
When a package variant is in any binary state other than a build-required state, it should not appear in the reduced recipe-ordered build-order output.
When a recipe still has build-required work after reduction, its position and dependency ordering in the build-order output should remain unchanged.

task_15.title: Avoid self-referential build-profile tool requirements
task_15.description: Conan 2.14.0 fixes dependency graph construction for build-profile `[tool_requires]` so a tool package does not add itself as its own tool requirement when referenced directly or through a matching version range. This prevents self-loops while preserving normal tool requirement resolution for other cases.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that build-profile `[tool_requires]` entries do not create a self-dependency or graph loop when a tool package matches itself, including when the self-reference is expressed as a version range.

expectation.grounded: When Conan applies `[tool_requires]` from a build profile during dependency graph construction, it should ignore a tool requirement whose package identity matches the current package and whose version is either exactly the same as the current package version or a version range satisfied by the current package version. Other tool requirements should continue to be registered normally.
expectation.conceptual: Build-profile tool requirements should never cause a package to depend on itself. Self-references must be skipped whether they are written as the same version or as a version range that resolves to the current package, while valid non-self tool requirements remain unaffected.

constraints.grounded: The change should only suppress true self-referential tool requirements in build context. Exact self-references must remain ignored, and entries for different package identities or same-package version expressions that do not match the current version should retain existing behavior.
constraints.conceptual: Only real self-dependency loops should be blocked. Unrelated tool requirements and valid alternative-version requirements should continue to resolve as before.

behavior: A build-profile `[tool_requires]` entry that targets the same package identity and exact version as the current tool package is ignored instead of being added again.
A build-profile `[tool_requires]` entry that targets the same package identity through a version range is ignored when the current package version falls within that range.
A same-package version-ranged tool requirement is not suppressed solely because the package names match; it is only skipped when the current package version satisfies the declared range.
Dependency graph construction should avoid introducing a self-loop from build-profile tool requirements in these self-matching cases.
acceptance_criteria: When a build profile declares a `[tool_requires]` entry for the same tool package and version currently being processed, dependency resolution should skip that entry and continue without creating a self-dependency.

When a build profile declares a `[tool_requires]` entry for the same tool package using a version range that includes the current package version, dependency resolution should skip that entry and avoid a graph loop.

When a build profile declares a `[tool_requires]` entry for a different package, or for the same package with a version expression that does not match the current version, the tool requirement should still participate in normal resolution.
Upgrading to 2.14.0 should eliminate the self-loop behavior for matching self-referential build-profile tool requirements without changing unrelated tool requirement handling.
